items.review_rationale: Reviewed graph isomorphism as bijective vertex map preserving and reflecting unordered adjacency, assuming both graph inputs simple and undirected and distinct-vertex condition.

references.phrase: simple undirected graphs G and H

references.context: Function injective and surjective on the entire target vertex set.
For every distinct u,v, edge {u,v} occurs in G exactly when {f(u),f(v)} occurs in H.
Edges are two-element subsets, without orientation or loops.

references.disposition: Preservation alone is insufficient; reflection and bijectivity are required.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed rational modulus by piecewise sign in rational total order, avoiding square-root definitions or dependence on constructed real numbers.

references.context: Order relation comparing rationals from their integer-fraction representations.
Result equals q when q>=0 and additive inverse -q when q<0.
Subset of Q consisting of zero together with positive rationals.

references.disposition: Definition uses rational ordering and negation only.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed rationals as field of fractions of integer ring with nonzero integer denominators and cross multiplication criterion for fraction equality.

references.context: Integer denominator q not equal to zero of Z.
Cross multiplication criterion for equality of integer fractions p/q and r/s with nonzero denominators.

references.phrase: rational field not real number construction
references.disposition: This definition is closed over integer arithmetic and does not assume a real-number completion.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed rational sequences as functions from positive integers or specified natural-number subset to rational field, with positive full indexing for Cauchy construction.

references.context: Value of indexed function at positive integer n.

references.phrase: Cauchy sequences require entire positive index set
references.disposition: A partial-index sequence may be allowed generally, but full positive indexing is required for the specified infinite Cauchy construction.
